bibl.title: Practical guidelines for rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A THIRTY-AUTHOR CONSENSUS DEFINING WHAT COUNTS AS RIGOROUS in a field where thousands of preclinical studies produced exactly one unequivocal clinical translation - guidelines whose subject is the reliability of an evidence base, written by the people who produced it
span.quote: The potential for ischemic preconditioning to reduce infarct size was first recognized more than 30 years ago [ 180 ]. Despite extension of the concept to ischemic postconditioning [ 460 ] and remote ischemic conditioning [ 202 , 344 ] and literally thousands of experimental studies in various species and models which identified a multitude of signaling steps [ 199 ], so far there is only a single and very recent study, which has unequivocally translated cardioprotection to improved clinical outcome as the primary endpoint in patients

span.label: what design, conduct, analysis and reporting practices would make cardioprotection studies reproducible enough to be worth translating
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: practical guidelines covering study design, randomisation, blinding, power, statistics, each experimental model with its own limitations, the omics technologies, and the design of clinical proof-of-concept and outcome trials
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: method
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: a field that cannot replicate itself, writing down what it will count as rigour
span.quote: In this context, it is disconcerting that the CAESAR consortium (Consortium for preclinicAl assESsment of cARdioprotective therapies) in a highly standardized multi-center approach of preclinical studies identified only ischemic preconditioning, but not nitrite or sildenafil, when given as adjunct to reperfusion, to reduce infarct size

span.label: expert consensus of the EU-CARDIOPROTECTION COST Action, approved by its management committee, building on the ARRIVE and ICH E9/E6 guidelines
span.term: expert consensus of the EU-CARDIOPROTECTION COST Action, approved by its management committee, building on the ARRIVE and ICH E9/E6 guidelines
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: THE PAPER DEFINES ITS OWN TWO WORDS AND MAKES ONE DEPEND ON THE OTHER: `we DEFINE RIGOR AS STANDARDIZED STATE-OF-THE-ART DESIGN, CONDUCT AND REPORTING OF A STUDY, WHICH IS THEN A PREREQUISITE FOR REPRODUCIBILITY, i.e. REPLICATION OF RESULTS BY ANOTHER LABORATORY WHEN PERFORMING EXACTLY THE SAME EXPERIMENT.` Rigour is a property of the doing; reproducibility is a property of what happens next, somewhere else
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: AND THE FAILURE THAT MOTIVATES IT IS COUNTED: `literally THOUSANDS OF EXPERIMENTAL STUDIES in various species and models ... so far there is ONLY A SINGLE AND VERY RECENT STUDY, which has UNEQUIVOCALLY TRANSLATED cardioprotection to improved clinical outcome as the primary endpoint in patients`
span.quote: The potential for ischemic preconditioning to reduce infarct size was first recognized more than 30 years ago [ 180 ]. Despite extension of the concept to ischemic postconditioning [ 460 ] and remote ischemic conditioning [ 202 , 344 ] and literally thousands of experimental studies in various species and models which identified a multitude of signaling steps [ 199 ], so far there is only a single and very recent study, which has unequivocally translated cardioprotection to improved clinical outcome as the primary endpoint in patients

span.label: AND A STANDARDISED MULTI-CENTRE REPLICATION FOUND ONE EFFECT OF THREE: `the CAESAR consortium ... in a HIGHLY STANDARDIZED MULTI-CENTER APPROACH of preclinical studies identified ONLY ISCHEMIC PRECONDITIONING, BUT NOT NITRITE OR SILDENAFIL, when given as adjunct to reperfusion, to reduce infarct size`
span.quote: In this context, it is disconcerting that the CAESAR consortium (Consortium for preclinicAl assESsment of cARdioprotective therapies) in a highly standardized multi-center approach of preclinical studies identified only ischemic preconditioning, but not nitrite or sildenafil, when given as adjunct to reperfusion, to reduce infarct size

span.label: AND TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE NAMED TEST GIVE DIFFERENT ANSWERS: `Caveat - DIFFERENT STATISTICAL SOFTWARE PACKAGES WORK WITH SLIGHTLY DIFFERENT ASSUMPTIONS AND CAN COME TO DIFFERENT OUTCOMES, as demonstrated for the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney`. Third consecutive record in this corpus where one construct measured two ways gives two answers - zook2016's aligners, ainsworth2020's five assays, and now a statistical test that has a name and a citation
span.quote: Caveat—different statistical software packages work with slightly different assumptions and can come to different outcomes, as demonstrated for the Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney

span.label: AND THE SURROGATES DO NOT PREDICT THE THING THEY STAND IN FOR, with the real definition arriving in a parenthesis immediately afterwards: `NONE of the above-mentioned variable/surrogate endpoints IS INDEED PREDICTIVE OF CLINICAL OUTCOMES in patients with acute myocardial infarction, i.e. truly indicative of `cardioprotection` (WHICH IS PRIMARILY INFARCT SIZE REDUCTION)`
span.quote: None of the above-mentioned variable/surrogate endpoints is indeed predictive of clinical outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction, i.e. truly indicative of “cardioprotection” (which is primarily infarct size reduction).

span.label: AND ONE DRUG IS THE COMMON DENOMINATOR OF THE FAILURES: `propofol SPECIFICALLY ABROGATES THE PROTECTION by remote ischemic conditioning in patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass graft surgery ... and SEEMS TO BE A COMMON DENOMINATOR OF ALL STUDIES THAT FAILED TO SEE PROTECTION`. A confounder that explains a literature's negative results, named
span.quote: Propofol seems no more cardioprotective than isoflurane per se, but in contrast to isoflurane and sevoflurane, propofol specifically abrogates the protection by remote ischemic conditioning in patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass graft surgery [ 32 , 260 , 261 , 454 ], and seems to be a common denominator of all studies that failed to see protection

span.label: the choice of statistical test follows the shape of the data, not the field: one endpoint at one time point takes a t test or one-way ANOVA, sequential measurements take a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA
span.quote: When comparing just a single endpoint at one single time point, a Student t test is appropriate for comparison of two groups; for more than two groups, a one-way ANOVA with subsequent tests for pairwise comparisons of mean values is appropriate.

span.label: an improving standard of care raises the sample size a trial needs, because the event rate the intervention must beat keeps falling
span.quote: Current cardioprotection studies in patients undergoing reperfusion for STEMI are challenged by the excellent outcome with modern standard therapy.

span.label: the assumed effect size is imported from proof-of-concept studies - a 25% reduction in events is rationalised by 30% reductions in infarct size reported earlier
span.quote: An effect size of 25% relative reduction in the event rate is rationalized by proof-of-concept clinical studies, in which remote ischemic conditioning was reported to induce 30% reductions in infarct size [ 185 ].

span.label: THE INSTRUMENT DECIDES WHAT IS FOUND, STATED THREE TIMES IN THREE TECHNOLOGIES. RNA: `it is NOT RECOMMENDED TO USE DIFFERENT KITS IN THE SAME STUDY, since SOME WILL FAVOR THE ISOLATION OF SHORT RNAs WHILE OTHERS WILL ENRICH THE RNA FRACTION WITH LONG MOLECULES`
span.quote: Due to the different kind of kits, it is not recommended to use different kits in the same study, since some will favor the isolation of short RNAs while others will enrich the RNA fraction with long molecules.

span.label: proteomics: `the LARGE ABUNDANCE PROTEINS MASK THE CHANGES OF LOW-ABUNDANCE PROTEINS which also make a significant contribution to cellular signalling` - and the targeted alternative `LOSES THE UNBIASED FEATURE of proteomics`. Coverage and accuracy traded against each other, explicitly
span.quote: This results in the major limitation of unbiased proteomics analysis, i.e. the large abundance proteins mask the changes of low-abundance proteins which also make a significant contribution to cellular signalling.

span.label: and multiomics software: `their DIVERSITY IN MATHEMATICAL MODELS AND SOURCE DATA DO NOT YET ALLOW ACCURATE COMPARISON OF DIFFERENT RESULTS`
span.quote: Analysis of multiomics data (target predictions, pathway analyses) needs excessive bioinformatic expertise. However, user-friendly software is rapidly emerging, but their diversity in mathematical models and source data do not yet allow accurate comparison of different results.

span.label: AND THERE IS NO ACCEPTED METHOD FOR MISSING VALUES, QUOTED FROM SOMEBODY ELSE RATHER THAN ASSERTED: `Unfortunately, there is `NO METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH FOR HANDLING MISSING VALUES THAT IS UNIVERSALLY ACCEPTED IN ALL SITUATIONS``
span.quote: Missing values can bias the results. In the presence of many missing values, the ability to draw valid conclusions is seriously compromised. Unfortunately, there is “no methodological approach for handling missing values that is universally accepted in all situations

span.label: AND A COMMON PRACTICE IS REFUSED FOR A REASON THAT IS A ZERO-CLAIM ABOUT AN INSTRUMENT: `pretests are performed to test data for normality ... Those pretests CANNOT BE RECOMMENDED, since THE FAILURE TO REJECT THE NULL HYPOTHESIS DOES NOT IMPLY THAT THE NULL HYPOTHESIS HOLDS, in particular since THE POWER OF THE PRETESTS IS OFTEN LOW`
span.quote: In some applications, pretests are performed to test data for normality or to test for homogeneity of variances. Those pretests cannot be recommended, since the failure to reject the null hypothesis does not imply that the null hypothesis holds, in particular since the power of the pretests is often low.

span.label: AND THE CHOICE OF DESIGN IS ADMITTED TO BE A COMPROMISE RATHER THAN A STANDARD: `The selection of the design ... ALWAYS REPRESENTS A COMPROMISE OF A MOST RIGOROUS APPROACH VS. LIMITED RESOURCES AND FEASIBILITY. Clearly, an EXPLORATORY study, while AIMING FOR NOVELTY, is associated with A GREATER RISK OF FALSE-POSITIVE FINDINGS ... whereas a PROSPECTIVE study aims for an existing specific hypothesis but PROVIDES MORE ROBUST DATA`
span.quote: The selection of the design (observational/exploratory vs. prospective) for a given project always represents a compromise of a most rigorous approach vs. limited resources and feasibility. Clearly, an exploratory study, while aiming for novelty, is associated with a greater risk of false-positive findings due to confounding factors, whereas a prospective study aims for an existing specific hypothesis but provides more robust data.

span.label: and two authors of a rigour guideline hold commercial interests in the field, declared: shareholders in a company and a founder-CEO of a group of R&D companies. Not a defect - a disclosure, and it belongs next to the paper's subject the way hoste2006's `SOME MEMBERS OF OUR RESEARCH GROUP HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE CONSENSUS PROCESS BY WHICH RIFLE WAS DEVELOPED` does
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: cardiac mortality has fallen steadily for 25 years and is now very low, so the outcome a cardioprotection trial must improve on is already excellent
span.quote: Cardiac mortality at 12 months has decreased continuously over the last 25 years [ 368 ] and is now below 6% [ 126 ], while rehospitalisation for heart failure is 8% [ 126 ].

span.label: a clinical outcome trial on the composite endpoint needs patients in the thousands per arm, which the paper spells out rather than leaving implicit
span.quote: To demonstrate a 25% reduction in the primary composite endpoint in the intervention group (from 8.0 to 6.0%), with 80% power and at the 5% significance level, will require 2554 patients/treatment arm which equates to 5108 patients in total.

span.label: reduction of the biochemical marker by the intervention has ranged from no effect at all to a large reduction across previous studies
span.quote: The reduction of biochemical marker release by a cardioprotective intervention has varied from no effect to up to 43% reduction by remote ischemic conditioning in previous studies [ 202 ].

span.label: stratified analyses must carry their own power calculations, or the stratification is not valid
span.quote: Power calculations must be provided to ensure the validity of the stratified analyses.

span.label: pre-specified inclusion and exclusion criteria, blinding, randomisation and a power calculation before the experiment starts
span.note: eliminates: post-hoc adjustment of the study to its own result - stated as a prohibition: `IT IS NOT PERMITTED to change the sample size post hoc, to add a new randomized group, or to supplement additional experiments` · outcome: held
span.quote: When the analysis of the experiment results in no or only a borderline significance, it is not permitted to change the sample size post hoc, to add a new randomized group, or to supplement additional experiments.

span.label: pretests for normality or homogeneity of variance before choosing a test
span.note: eliminates: nothing, and the paper refuses the practice: `Those pretests CANNOT BE RECOMMENDED, since THE FAILURE TO REJECT THE NULL HYPOTHESIS DOES NOT IMPLY THAT THE NULL HYPOTHESIS HOLDS` · outcome: failed
span.quote: In some applications, pretests are performed to test data for normality or to test for homogeneity of variances. Those pretests cannot be recommended, since the failure to reject the null hypothesis does not imply that the null hypothesis holds, in particular since the power of the pretests is often low.

span.label: a consensus re-read when two human readers disagree about infarct size by more than 3%
span.note: eliminates: reader-dependent infarct size on the primary endpoint - a disagreement threshold that triggers a procedure rather than an argument · outcome: held
span.quote: If the difference in infarct size between the readers exceeds 3%, a consensus reading is recommended from the two or additional readers.

span.label: a surrogate endpoint that predicts clinical outcome
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the paper says none exists: `NONE of the above-mentioned variable/surrogate endpoints IS INDEED PREDICTIVE OF CLINICAL OUTCOMES` · outcome: absent-not-in-staged-text
span.quote: None of the above-mentioned variable/surrogate endpoints is indeed predictive of clinical outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction, i.e. truly indicative of “cardioprotection” (which is primarily infarct size reduction).

span.label: rigor
span.quote: We refer to the recent guidelines for experimental models of myocardial ischemia and infarction [ 279 ], and aim to provide now practical guidelines to ensure rigor and reproducibility in preclinical and clinical studies on cardioprotection. In line with the above guidelines [ 279 ], we define rigor as standardized state-of-the-art design, conduct and reporting of a study, which is then a prerequisite for reproducibility, i.e. replication of results by another laboratory when performing exactly the same experiment.

span.label: hazard ratio

span.label: multiplicity

span.label: effect size

span.label: `outlier` - operationalised by Tukey's fences rather than by judgement: data outside `first quartile - 1.5 inter-quartile range and third quartile + 1.5 inter-quartile range`
span.quote: The “whiskers” of the full box plot according to Tukey’s [ 428 ] original definition extend to the most extreme data within the inner fences, that is, first quartile—1.5 inter-quartile range and third quartile + 1.5 inter-quartile range. Data outside the inner fences, i.e. data points outside of the range depicted by the box and whiskers, are considered outliers.

span.label: `primary variable` - `the variable capable of providing THE MOST RELEVANT AND CONVINCING EVIDENCE DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE of the trial`, quoted from ICH E9, with `ideally there is only one primary endpoint`
span.quote: According to the ICH E9 guideline [ 168 ], the primary variable “should be the variable capable of providing the most relevant and convincing evidence directly related to the primary objective of the trial”. This is also true for experimental studies, and ideally there is only one primary endpoint.
